Ken Martin.title: Anything
Ken Martin.about:
This track is dedicated to my late brother Brian. Brian, despite his physical "limitations", pursued every adventure that popped up along his path. His mind was open and willing to try new things, his spirit was gentle and humble, his heart was strong and brave. His name, Brian Martin actually means Strong Warrior, a fitting title for someone who proved beyond a shadow of a doubt, that he could do anything he put his heart to.
If you knew Brian, you know that his strength and capabilities are not embellished in the stories you hear of him. And if you didn't know Brian...well, sorry mate. You really missed out on knowing one of the most overachieving individuals who ever graced the planet.
I hope this song serves as inspiration for all who hear it. As corny as it sounds, you are capable of achieving all of your dreams. Heck you are capable of surpassing your own expectations! You can do anything!
Your dreams are already actualized; they're just waiting for you to catch up to that reality!

Ken Martin.title: Inside My Head
Ken Martin.about:
This past week was a little deep. I'm a deep thinker by nature, but this past week had me thinking deeper than usual.
I watched the documentary "Chimp Empire" On Netflix. In this docu-series viewers are introduced to a chimp named Gus. Gus is part of a group of chimps that has over 120 members. Sadly, despite all of the members in this particular chimp group, Gus is a loner and outsider.
Often rejected when it comes to being groomed by other chimps, a highly political and extremely important aspect of chimp to chimp connection, communication, and socializing, Gus is is isolated, which can be dangerous for a chimp's physical, social, and emotional well being. I don't think I've ever identified more with a character in my life.
Things do start going well for Gus eventually, but seeing his lonely state helped inspire some of this song. I've always loved primates, except humans (jk), and this song reminds of an image of Gus sitting alone and dejected at the base of a tree just thinking. Seeing him make attempts to make friends and fail really strikes home. As an altruist, I always want everyone to be happy, have friends, and be included; even our primate cousins.
Love You, Gus!

Ken Martin.title: Lift Each Other Up
Ken Martin.about:
To all of the Brothers and Sisters of Humanity,
A family is like a group of trees, whether that group is a forest, a jungle, or just a few trees scattered throughout the park or along the street. The better the environment for the trees to grow, the better the trees can positively impact their environment. However, trees don't only impact the space that they occupy. They also impact every man, woman, and child that passes by them. Whether or not the passersby are one Happy Family or are lone travelers, the trees are somehow impacting the travelers' journey. Even when the positive impact of the trees from all around the world is not immediately recognized, the oversight in recognition does not diminish the necessity of the trees and their usefulness.
Happy Families impact the world in greater ways than one might think. Happy Families have codes of ethics that keep each other in check. If there is a Happy Family who has a son who is also a Brother to a Sister or a Brother, and he comes up short in maintaining the standards and ethics of the family code, he is held accountable by either his Brother or his Sister. If he has maintained the code, and he himself also has a Brother, then he will he see to it that his Brother is held accountable as well, for Brothers hold each other accountable. When he is taught from an early age how to maintain the family code, he grows into a man who will carry the practices which he learned from his youth into adulthood. He will remember that he will be held accountable for his actions and behaviors, and that he must hold other Men and Brothers accountable for theirs as well.
When a Happy Family has a daughter who is also a Sister to a Brother or a Sister, she too bares the same previously mentioned responsibilities as the afore mentioned Brother. A Sister's responsibility is no less important than a Brother's when it comes to maintaining the code of familial accountability. A Sister both speaks up for her Sister, if she has one, and speaks up to her Brother, if she has to. In a Happy Family with children, siblings are responsible for holding each other to the highest standards and the best practices that they've been taught from their childhood; The Brothers are there for their Brothers AND their Sisters, and the Sisters are there for their Sisters AND their Brothers.
When Siblings hurt each other and are not held accountable, it is because they have forgotten The Rule, which is the cornerstone of a Happy Family; To Love Each Other. When The Rule is not upheld, a Happy Family must come together to restore order. Someone MUST speak up. Someone MUST listen. Someone MUST be held accountable. The only hope for a Happy Family who's siblings have hurt each other is if the The Rule, To Love Each Other, is embedded deep within the hearts and minds of the siblings of that family from an early age.
When the children of Happy Families are taught early in life to love each other, they are given the opportunity to experience two of the greatest needs that children thrive upon; the opportunity to both learn AND play. Happy Families teach their children that loving each other includes speaking up for each other when the one being spoken for could be or has been hurt, and speaking up to each other when the actions of the one being spoken to could lead to or have led to another being hurt. The sooner Brothers and Sisters are taught to love each other in this way, the sooner they learn that they themselves, along with others, are going to be held accountable for their actions
When Brothers and Sisters of Happy Families expand their families by making friends, finding social community, entering into marriage, or deciding to have children of their own, they will carry with them the same standards and code of family ethics that they were taught when they were children. They will speak up for and to their friends, their communities, their spouses, and their children if or whenever the need arises, and by doing so, they will demonstrate how to love each other.
When a Brother or Sister of a Happy Family has been harmed by one of their own members, a Happy Family will come together to protect AND correct itself. Every member must be held accountable for the participation or lack there of in the situation that has caused the harm.
..."Did someone see the one who caused the harm? Did someone stop the guilty person while that person was on their way to do harm? Did someone see the guilty person caring out the harmful actions? Was the guilty person called out in the moment and held accountable? Did someone see or hear the one who was hurt? Did someone come to defend the one who was hurt either before, in the moment, or at least after the hurt was inflicted? Did someone listen to the one who was hurt when the hurt person told their side of the story?"...
Saying yes or no to any of these questions can mean many different things for the Brother or Sister answering the question based off of their involvement, or lack thereof, in the situation.
When a member of a Happy Family is hurt, the entire family is hurt as well. If happiness can be felt together by the whole unit, then hurt can also be felt together by the whole unit. The tears of one must be spread out equally, and must be felt and expressed by all within the family. A Happy Family is not only defined by its ability to enjoy happiness together, but also by its willingness to embrace tears and sorrow together because that is something that a Happy Family would do, happily. Tears of hurt and tears of guilt are to be shared and expressed even with those who have not been directly hurt or who are not guilty of hurting others. Crying together helps Brothers and Sisters heal, and helps Brothers and Sisters heal each other. When Brothers and Sisters cry together in an attempt to heal each other, they don't always shed tears, but they ALWAYS take action!
When a Brother hurts one of our Sisters, it is the responsibility of ALL of the Brothers throughout the world to cry with our Sisters by taking action and holding our Brother accountable. The smallest infraction is worth discussing. Brothers, speak up for our Sisters by speaking up to the Brothers who hurt our Sisters. No Brother wants to be spoken down to, so before we see a Brother fall, we need to speak up to him. Encourage him. Love him. Lift him up. Let him know about the positive impact of his good actions and behaviors and do not shy away from discussing the pain that can stem from his negative actions and behaviors.
Brothers, we are all one family. Let us help our Brothers and heal our Sisters. Let us take each others' suffering seriously. When our Sisters tell us that there is something fundamentally wrong with our behavior listen, reflect, and act. Sisters, never stop telling us when we are off the mark and let us know when we have done well so we can form patterns of respectful behavior towards our Sisters that our children's children's children will experience.
We are all one family. Let us love each other so that we may be a Happy Family.

Ken Martin.title: Mother's Day - Demo
Ken Martin.about:
Hey Ya'll,
This song is a demo track from my upcoming album which currently has no title, theme, or release date. This track is just me debuting my drumming skills. Yeah, that's me on them drums. Could be a little cleaner, but I had a blast writing and playing this song regardless. Really excited to be at a point where I'm playing every last sound you hear on the track.
This is also my first song I've written and shared with regards to anything mother related. I mean it kind of makes sense; it is Mother's Day after all. So play this song for your mother if she still walks among us in the land of the living.
Currently this song will only be featured on Bandcamp until the full album is completed and released on other streaming services such as Spotify, Apple Music, or just about wherever else you stream your music.
Hope you all enjoy!
Ken Martin
